name: Wisconsin
summary_text: Visitors to Wisconsin stand under the national framework of the United States. Executive Order 14168 of 20 January 2025 redefined sex for federal purposes as a male-female binary and barred self-selection of gender on passports and visas; the State Department has stopped processing the X marker and issues new passports only as M or F from supporting documents, while passports already holding an X marker remain valid until expiry. The Supreme Court allowed those restrictions to take effect in November 2025, and by March 2025 trans and nonbinary travellers reported passports confiscated or blocked at processing, with some left stranded abroad.  Entry screening carries a separate exposure. An executive order of 5 February 2025 and a State Department announcement of 25 February 2025 provide for refusing visas to trans athletes seeking entry to compete in women's sports, flagging visa applicants with an internal marking and treating as fraud, with a permanent bar, any applicant listing a gender other than the one assigned at birth. Transportation Security Administration checkpoint procedures involve secondary screening, hand-held devices and pat-downs that can be invasive of privacy and risk outing a trans traveller.  At state level, Wisconsin is grouped among the low-risk states. A national legal-risk assessment of July 2026 placed Wisconsin in its 'Low-Risk States' group alongside Arizona, Delaware, Maine, Michigan, Nevada, Pennsylvania, Virginia and the District of Columbia, describing such jurisdictions as having largely refrained from targeting transgender adults while not taking extraordinary steps to protect them. The second half of that formulation matters: the assessment records no Wisconsin statute restricting where trans people may be, and no state-level protection of comparable weight to the federal measures described above.  Wisconsin has no state ban on gender-affirming care for minors. Governor Tony Evers vetoed Assembly Bill 465 on 6 December 2023, blocking a measure that would have restricted such care; the Human Rights Campaign stated that the veto kept the restriction from taking effect in the state.  Wisconsin has no state ban on trans school athletes either. On 2 April 2024 Governor Evers vetoed a bill passed by the Republican-controlled Legislature that would have limited high school athletes to teams matching the sex assigned at birth. The bill's sponsor called the veto 'disgusting'; the Associated Press reported that Evers had promised the veto when the bill was introduced and that Democrats did not have the votes to stop its passage in the Legislature.  Care access is nonetheless constrained by federal funding pressure rather than state law. On 13 January 2026 UW Health and Children's Wisconsin each announced a pause on gender-affirming pharmacologic care for patients under 18, after the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services said it would deny Medicaid and Medicare payments to hospitals providing such care to minors. Mental and behavioural health services continued. Wisconsin Attorney General Josh Kaul joined a coalition of states seeking to block the HHS declaration.  Official hostility at federal level extends to enforcement machinery. In December 2025 the attorney general instructed the FBI to offer cash bounties for information leading to the identification and arrest of transgender activists promoting what she called radical gender ideology, describing such activists as domestic terrorist groups, and a May 2026 national counterterrorism strategy stated that counterterrorism activity would prioritise the rapid identification and neutralisation of groups whose ideology is described as anti-American, radically pro-transgender and anarchist.  Custody carries documented harm. From 2026 the Federal Bureau of Prisons adopted Florida-based policies for transgender inmates that mandate cutting their hair short, withdrawing hormone medication and substituting psychiatric therapy and psychiatric drugs; imprisoned transgender people reported being denied care, and the Bureau of Prisons stopped reporting the number of transgender prisoners it holds from 2025. In immigration detention, transgender men were subjected to forced-labour programmes with guards justifying them by saying they would treat them 'like a man,' and those who refused faced beatings and solitary confinement, alongside widely reported severe sexual abuse.
